messages:
sam: heads-up — opened a tiny PR against the ruby client to change auth header handling. CI failed in one job, not sure if it's flaky or a real bug. https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/82 :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
laura: link? quick glance pls, we try to keep ruby parity with js for retries/auth.
mike: seeing this — the failing test looks like `auth_header` normalization expects `Bearer <token>` but our gem sometimes sends raw token when KMS refresh hook is used.
chandra: are we sure it's the gem? could be sample app using middleware incorrectly. which CI job failed?
sam: `ruby-ci-bot` job: unit/rack-integration (matrix: ruby-3.1). stack trace showed middleware inserted twice in test helper. minimal repro in spec attached.
laura: hmm. Sam — can you paste the minimal repro here? a one-file example helps me triage.
sam: sure, pasted snippet:
```
# spec/helpers/auth_helper.rb
use Rack::Builder.new do
  use Redwood::Auth::Middleware, token_provider: -> { ENV['RW_TOKEN'] }
  run TestApp
end
```
laura: ok that looks fine. The difference is our middleware previously accepted `token:` or `authorization:` key in options; we tightened to always set `Authorization` header. Some older sample apps relied on Behavior A.
mike: that explains onboarding friction — new users hit this when following the tutorial. We should either revert to backward-compatible accept-or-normalize behavior or update docs and throw a clear warning in middleware.
chandra: +1 for normalization. Small change but avoids user pain. Can we add a deprecation warning for users passing token in alternate key?
jen: also: PR review backlog is getting long for community SDKs. We should decide a maintenance policy: minimal support for community SDKs (bugfixes/security) vs active feature parity. It affects how quickly we respond to changes like this.
sam: proposal: maintainers triage weekly. Bugfixes & CI flakes prioritized, feature parity on a best-effort basis unless signaled by product.
laura: sounds reasonable. For this PR I can do a quick patch: accept old keys, normalize to `Authorization: Bearer ...`, emit a single warn once (use RSpec to silence in tests). Will add changelog entry.
mike: please also add a tiny integration test that mimics sample app flow — bundler + minimal Rack app. That will catch regressions.
jen: and update the quickstart in docs repo — the snippet in `dev-quickstarts/ruby.md` still shows the older pattern. If we normalize behavior we should keep docs showing the canonical usage and call out migration note.
chandra: CI note: ruby-ci-bot runs the gem build then matrix tests. If we add the deprecation warn, ensure `--warnings` doesn't break CI. Use logger.warn instead of STDERR.
laura: good call. I'll open a follow-up commit on the PR with:
- normalization + logger.warn
- unit test for token variants
- integration spec for minimal sample app
- CHANGELOG entry and docs PR link in description

sam: amazing, thanks! assign me if you want me to iterate on CI fixes.
mike: assign to laura and tag `ruby-maintainers` team. I'll queue review but can only do quick look due to release week. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jen: for the maintenance policy, I'll create a short GH issue in the infra repo to formalize weekly triage and on-call rotation for community SDKs. If anyone wants to be on rotation, reply in that issue.
sam: one small question — how do we handle semver bumps for these small fixes? patch-only?
laura: patch release (0.6.x -> 0.6.x+1). We'll follow semantic-minimal: bugfix -> patch, behavior change with deprecation -> minor with migration note.
mike: FYI community user reported similar on Discord earlier, so good to get a quick patch out.
chandra: ok PR updated, CI rerun in 5m.
ruby-ci-bot: run results: matrix: pass on ruby-3.1, ruby-3.2; flake on jruby job retried and passed. :white_check_mark:
sam: thanks everyone — this is a nice small win for onboarding friction. I'll update the sample app in `examples/ruby/simple-chat` after release. :rocket!
